program_overview.title: Full Stack Web Development for Teens
program_overview.tagline: One honest stack, learned deeply: from a first hand-typed page to a deployed application with accounts, a database, live chat and an AI feature.
program_overview.description:
Full stack means owning both halves of an application: the frontend people see and the backend that quietly runs it. This live online course takes students aged 13 to 18 from an empty folder to exactly that, a real deployed application with user accounts, a database, real-time features and an AI-powered capability, built with the stack that dominates modern development: JavaScript, React, Node.js and MongoDB, with SQL and TypeScript where the industry expects them.

The arc is deliberate. Three months of true foundations: HTML, CSS, layouts that survive a phone screen, then JavaScript learned properly, including the asynchronous side that separates real developers from tutorial followers. Three months of React, the way it is actually written in 2026: hooks, routing, TypeScript, a taste of Next.js, and a frontend capstone. Three months of backend: Node and Express, MongoDB and SQL, authentication done safely, and an API deployed to a public URL. The final three months put the halves together: file uploads, live chat with Socket.io, AI features built with proper guardrails, testing, and a four-week capstone shipped like a product.

The pace is honest: two live classes a week plus three to four hours of practice fits this in twelve months, and students who need longer take up to fourteen, the class adapts instead of rushing. Learning is checked the honest way too: homework after every class, monthly assignments that mix new questions with earlier topics, and a final exam that decides the certificate. Real knowledge, real work, real projects, depth over dopamine.
what_makes_this_different: One stack learned deeply instead of four frameworks skimmed: JavaScript, React, Node and MongoDB, with SQL and TypeScript where industry expects them
Everything ships: projects go to real public URLs from month 3 onward, not screenshots on a laptop
AI is built, not bolted on: students add AI features to their own apps with streaming, guardrails and cost control
An honest 12-month arc with 2 months of margin built in: students who need more practice take up to 14, nobody is rushed
Small live batches capped at 10 students, with mini-batch and 1-on-1 options for closer attention
Real assessment: weekly homework, mixed-review assignments every month, and a final exam that decides the certificate, with focused revision and a free retest for students who fall short

faqs.question: What will my teen build in this full stack course?
faqs.answer: More than 30 real projects across twelve months, each phase ending with something deployed: a multi-page API-powered site in month 3, a polished React frontend capstone in month 6, an authenticated API and full-stack app in month 9, and a final capstone with user accounts, a database, live chat and an AI-powered feature, live on its own URL. Every project is built by the student and reviewed with written feedback.

faqs.question: How long does it take a teenager to learn full stack development?
faqs.answer: Full stack is genuinely the biggest track we teach, both halves of an application, so the honest answer is 12 months at 2 live classes a week plus 3 to 4 hours of practice. The syllabus keeps 2 months of margin in hand: students who need more repetition take up to 14 months with no rushing and no penalty. The first deployed site goes live in month 3, so the motivation never has to wait.

faqs.question: How is my teen assessed? Is the certificate just for attending?
faqs.answer: No. Classwork runs inside every session, homework follows every class, and each month ends with an assignment that deliberately mixes new questions with earlier topics so knowledge compounds instead of fading. Every phase closes with a cumulative exam, and the course ends with a final exam: a practical build plus written questions drawn from the whole syllabus. Passing earns the certificate; falling short earns a focused revision plan and a free retest. We optimize for real knowledge and real depth, not a stream of feel-good badges.

faqs.question: Why React and Node instead of teaching many frameworks?
faqs.answer: Because depth beats a tour. React and Node dominate real-world hiring and share one language, JavaScript, so a teen’s effort compounds instead of splitting. We add TypeScript, SQL and a taste of Next.js because the industry expects them. A student who truly understands this one stack can pick up Vue, Angular or anything else in weeks, the concepts transfer; skimming four frameworks transfers nothing.

faqs.question: What does full stack actually mean?
faqs.answer: Frontend is everything users see and click; backend is the engine behind it: servers, databases, and logic. A full stack developer can build both, which is why this course covers the entire journey from a first webpage to a complete working application with accounts, data and live features.

faqs.question: Can a complete beginner join, and at what age?
faqs.answer: Yes, the course assumes zero coding knowledge and is designed for ages 13 to 18. The early months are deliberately gentle, real foundations before any framework, and batches are grouped by age and pace so nobody is racing or waiting.

faqs.question: How is AI part of this course?
faqs.answer: As a builder’s tool, in two layers: pre-trained models in the browser with TensorFlow.js, then AI features added to the student’s own full-stack app, model calls made safely from the server, streamed into React, with guardrails, cost control and honest evaluation. Where an AI service requires an account, it is set up together with a parent. The result is a teen who ships AI features, not one who only chats with AI.

faqs.question: What tools and costs are involved beyond the fee?
faqs.answer: None beyond a computer and internet: VS Code, Node.js, GitHub, React and every framework taught are free and open source. Projects are published on free hosting tiers, so student work is live on the real internet without extra cost.

faqs.question: How much are the monthly fees?
faqs.answer: Group classes are ₹1,499 per month, including 2 live classes a week in batches capped at 10 students. A mini batch of 3-4 students is ₹2,999 per month, and personal 1-on-1 classes are ₹4,999 per month. International students pay a price set for their own country, shown on this page in their local currency.

faqs.question: Does the course offer a free demo?
faqs.answer: Yes, book a free, no-commitment demo class at learn.modernagecoders.com/contact or message us on WhatsApp at +91 91233 66161. Parents are welcome to sit in; it is the easiest way to see whether the teaching style clicks for your teen.

faqs.question: What format do the classes follow?
faqs.answer: Live 1-hour online classes with a real teacher, never pre-recorded videos. Groups are small and hands-on: students build during class, ask questions, and get unstuck immediately.

faqs.question: Will my teen be certified at the end?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it is earned, not handed out: the certificate is awarded on passing the final exam, with a free retest after revision if the first attempt falls short. More importantly, they finish holding a portfolio of deployed applications, live products that prove the certificate means something.
